metadata.title: UI Design Library — Component & Design System Reference
metadata.description: A curated library of UI components and design systems from component.gallery, enriched with practical app-building guidance using Qwen3-VL-235B. Designed for rapid prototyping and vibe coding.

components.description: Accordions let users toggle between concise headers and detailed content without leaving the page, reducing visual clutter and improving scannability. Ideal for rapid prototyping when you need to hide secondary info behind intuitive triggers — perfect for 'vibe coding' where layout fluidity matters more than rigid structure.
use_cases: FAQ sections in landing pages
Settings panels with grouped options
Product feature breakdowns on e-commerce pages
Onboarding steps with expandable instructions
implementation_tips: Use CSS transitions for smooth open/close animations to enhance perceived performance.
Ensure only one panel expands at a time unless multi-expand is explicitly needed.
Add ARIA attributes (aria-expanded, aria-controls) for screen reader support.
components.accessibility_notes: Always include keyboard navigation (Enter/Space to toggle) and ensure focus management so users can tab through headers. Use semantic HTML (details/summary) or ARIA roles to convey state changes to assistive tech.
components.original_description: An accordion is a vertical stack of interactive headings used to toggle the display of further information; each item can be 'collapsed' with just a short label visible or 'expanded' to show the full content.

components.description: Alerts immediately draw user attention to critical updates, errors, or confirmations without disrupting workflow. Ideal for rapid prototyping to simulate real-world feedback loops—like form validation or system status—helping developers validate UX flow early and often.
use_cases: Form submission errors or success messages
System status updates (e.g., 'Saved', 'Offline')
Security warnings or permission prompts
Onboarding tips or feature highlights
implementation_tips: Auto-dismiss alerts after 5-7 seconds unless action is required.
Use color and iconography consistently to signal severity (red=error, green=success).
Ensure alerts are keyboard-navigable and don’t trap focus.
components.accessibility_notes: Include ARIA live regions for screen readers and ensure alerts are announced. Never rely solely on color to convey meaning.
components.original_description: A way of informing the user of important changes in a prominent way.

components.description: Avatars visually identify users in interfaces, reducing cognitive load by replacing abstract IDs with recognizable faces or initials. They enhance personalization and trust in social, collaborative, or account-based apps — critical for rapid prototyping where user context must be instantly clear.
use_cases: User profiles in dashboards
Comment sections in blogs or forums
Team member lists in project management tools
Chat or messaging interfaces
implementation_tips: Use fallback initials if no image is available to avoid broken UI.
Ensure consistent sizing and border radius across contexts for visual harmony.
components.accessibility_notes: Always include alt text for screen readers and ensure sufficient color contrast if using initials on colored backgrounds.
components.original_description: A graphical representation of a user: usually a photo, illustration, or initial.

components.description: Badges visually highlight status, counts, or metadata without cluttering the main UI—perfect for rapid prototyping to convey urgency, unread items, or state changes. They reduce cognitive load by drawing attention to key info without requiring extra clicks or navigation.
use_cases: Unread message counters in chat apps
Status indicators (e.g., 'New', 'Draft', 'Expired') on cards or lists
Feature tags in product dashboards (e.g., 'Beta', 'Pro')
Inventory stock levels (e.g., 'Low', 'Out of Stock') in e-commerce
implementation_tips: Use semantic color coding (e.g., red for errors, green for success) to reinforce meaning at a glance.
Limit badge text to 1-3 characters or use icons for space-constrained layouts.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure sufficient color contrast and include ARIA labels for screen readers to announce badge content, especially when conveying critical status.
components.original_description: A small label, generally appearing inside or in close proximity to another larger interface component, representing a status, property, or some other metadata.

components.description: Breadcrumbs help users understand their location within a multi-level app hierarchy and navigate back efficiently. They reduce cognitive load by providing context and quick escape routes, making them ideal for rapid prototyping of content-heavy or nested interfaces like e-commerce or documentation sites.
use_cases: Product category pages in e-commerce apps
Documentation or help center navigation
Admin dashboards with nested settings
File explorer or CMS content trees
implementation_tips: Use semantic HTML (nav + ol + li) for structure and SEO
Truncate long paths with ellipsis or collapse intermediate levels on mobile
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure each breadcrumb link is focusable and announced by screen readers; use aria-current='page' on the final item to indicate the current location.
components.original_description: A list of links showing the location of the current page in the navigational hierarchy.

components.description: Buttons are essential for triggering actions like form submission, navigation, or toggling UI states. They provide clear affordance for user interaction, reducing cognitive load and speeding up prototyping. In vibe coding, they let you quickly wire up flows without deep UX planning.
use_cases: Form submission in checkout flows
Toggle visibility of modals or sidebars
Initiate API calls (e.g., 'Save', 'Delete')
Navigation between app sections or screens
implementation_tips: Use semantic HTML <button> tags for native accessibility and keyboard support.
Add loading states for async actions to prevent double-clicks and improve feedback.
Apply consistent padding and hover/focus styles across your app for visual cohesion.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure buttons have visible focus states and ARIA labels if icon-only. Always include descriptive text for screen readers and support keyboard navigation (Enter/Space).
components.original_description: Buttons trigger an action such as submitting a form or showing/hiding an interface component.

components.description: A button group bundles related actions into a compact, visually cohesive unit—ideal for toolbars, filter toggles, or mode switches. It reduces cognitive load by grouping similar controls and improves layout efficiency, making it perfect for rapid prototyping where visual hierarchy matters.
use_cases: Toggle between view modes (list/grid) in dashboards
Filter options in data tables or search results
Action bars in mobile toolbars (e.g., undo/redo/share)
Segmented controls for switching between app sections
implementation_tips: Use consistent padding and spacing between buttons to avoid visual clutter.
Apply active state styling to indicate selection (e.g., background color or border).
Group with keyboard navigation support (arrow keys to cycle through buttons).
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure each button is focusable and announces its role/state via ARIA. Use semantic HTML (like <button> or role='button') and avoid divs for interactive elements.
components.original_description: A wrapper for multiple, related buttons.

components.description: Cards encapsulate related content into scannable, self-contained units that improve information hierarchy and user focus. Ideal for rapid prototyping, they let devs quickly wireframe lists of items (like products or tasks) while maintaining visual consistency and responsive behavior across screen sizes.
use_cases: Product listings in e-commerce apps
Task or to-do items in productivity tools
News or blog article previews
User profiles in social or team apps
implementation_tips: Use consistent padding and shadow depth to create visual rhythm and depth.
Add hover/focus states for interactive cards to signal tappable areas.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure cards with interactive elements (like buttons or links) are keyboard-navigable and announce their purpose via ARIA labels or semantic HTML.
components.original_description: A container for content representing a single entity. e.g. a contact, article, or task.

components.description: A carousel lets users browse multiple content panels (images, cards, testimonials) with intuitive swipe or button navigation. It saves screen space while keeping key content discoverable — ideal for hero sections, product showcases, or onboarding flows where visual storytelling matters.
use_cases: Hero banners on landing pages
Product image galleries in e-commerce
Testimonial sliders on marketing sites
Onboarding walkthroughs for mobile apps
implementation_tips: Auto-advance slides only if user is idle — avoid forcing motion on first load.
Add visible pagination dots or thumbnails so users know how many slides exist.
Ensure touch/swipe gestures work reliably on mobile with proper event handling.
components.accessibility_notes: Include keyboard navigation (left/right arrows), ARIA labels for slide position, and pause autoplay on focus to meet WCAG standards.
components.original_description: A means of displaying multiple slides of content, one or more at a time. Navigation between slides can be controlled via swiping, scrolling, or buttons.

components.description: A toggle input that lets users select one or more options from a predefined set. Essential for forms, filters, and settings — speeds up prototyping by reducing custom logic. Improves UX by making selections explicit and reversible without modal dialogs.
use_cases: User preference settings (e.g., email notifications)
Filtering lists (e.g., product categories)
Multi-select form fields (e.g., interests or permissions)
Feature toggles in admin dashboards
implementation_tips: Group related checkboxes with clear labels and use fieldsets for semantic structure.
Use CSS :checked pseudo-class for visual feedback without JS overhead.
Avoid nesting checkboxes inside buttons or links to prevent click confusion.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure each checkbox has a programmatically associated label via 'for' and 'id'. Use ARIA attributes if dynamically generated, and test keyboard navigation (Tab/Space).
components.original_description: An input for choosing from predefined options:

components.description: Allows users to select colors visually or via input, speeding up design customization in apps like themes, dashboards, or content editors. Reduces friction in creative workflows by replacing hex code guesswork with intuitive sliders or palettes.
use_cases: Custom theme builders in SaaS apps
Design tools for changing text/background colors
Dashboard widgets with user-defined color indicators
E-commerce product customization (e.g., shoe colors)
implementation_tips: Include both visual picker and hex/RGB input for power users
Default to a safe, accessible color palette to avoid poor contrast choices
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure keyboard navigation and screen reader support; provide contrast warnings if selected colors fail WCAG standards.
components.original_description: An input for choosing a color.

components.description: A hybrid input-select that lets users either type to filter options or pick from a dropdown—ideal for fast data entry with guidance. Reduces user friction in forms and search flows by combining discovery and precision, speeding up prototyping for apps needing smart inputs.
use_cases: User location or city selection in onboarding forms
Product or SKU search in e-commerce dashboards
Tag or category assignment in content management systems
Contact or team member selection in messaging apps
implementation_tips: Debounce input to avoid excessive API calls during typing
Highlight matching text fragments in dropdown options for visual clarity
Allow keyboard navigation (arrow keys, Enter) for accessibility and power users
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure screen readers announce filtered results and selected values. Use ARIA attributes like aria-expanded, aria-activedescendant, and role='combobox' to maintain semantic structure.
components.original_description: An input that behaves similarly to a select, with the addition of a free text input to filter options.

components.description: A date input lets users quickly select or type dates using structured fields (day/month/year) or a calendar picker, reducing input errors and improving form completion speed. Ideal for rapid prototyping of booking, scheduling, or filtering interfaces where date accuracy matters.
use_cases: Booking forms for hotels or flights
Event scheduling in calendar apps
Filtering data by date range in dashboards
Setting deadlines in task management tools
implementation_tips: Use native HTML5 <input type='date'> for basic needs with fallbacks for older browsers.
Pre-fill current date or suggest common ranges (e.g., ‘next week’) to reduce friction.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure keyboard navigation works across fields and screen readers announce labels clearly. Use ARIA attributes if customizing the picker.
components.original_description: A means of inputting a date – often separated into multiple individual fields for day/month/year.

components.description: A calendar-based UI that lets users select dates visually, reducing input errors and speeding up form completion. Ideal for rapid prototyping where date selection is critical—like booking or scheduling—because it’s intuitive and reduces validation logic needed on the backend.
use_cases: Booking systems (hotels, flights, appointments)
Event creation forms
Filtering data by date range in dashboards
Setting reminders or deadlines in productivity apps
implementation_tips: Pre-fill with today’s date or contextually relevant dates to reduce user effort.
Support keyboard navigation and arrow keys for quick date selection.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure screen reader compatibility by labeling the calendar grid and providing ARIA roles. Allow full keyboard navigation and focus management for users who can’t use a mouse.
pairs_well_with: Input field (for manual date entry fallback)
Tooltip (for date constraints or help text)
components.original_description: A visual way to choose a date using a calendar view.

components.description: A sliding panel that reveals secondary content without leaving the current screen, ideal for rapid prototyping of navigation, filters, or settings. It keeps core UI visible while reducing cognitive load and enabling quick context switching — perfect for vibe coding where flow matters more than fidelity.
use_cases: Side navigation menus on mobile or tablet
Filter panels in e-commerce or data dashboards
Settings or profile panels in apps
Contextual help or FAQ overlays
implementation_tips: Use hardware-accelerated transforms (translateX/translateY) for smooth sliding animations
Add a backdrop overlay to visually dim the main content and indicate focus shift
Support swipe-to-dismiss on mobile for intuitive gesture control
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure keyboard focus traps inside the drawer and announce its opening/closing via ARIA live regions. Provide a visible close button and escape key support.
components.original_description: A panel which slides out from the edge of the screen.

components.description: A dropdown menu reveals contextual actions or navigation options on demand, reducing clutter while keeping key functions accessible. Ideal for rapid prototyping, it lets devs quickly group related actions (like 'Edit', 'Delete', 'Share') without bloating the UI. Enhances user focus by hiding secondary options until needed.
use_cases: User profile action menus (e.g., Settings, Logout)
Contextual toolbars in content editors (e.g., Format, Insert)
Navigation overflow in mobile headers
Bulk action controls in data tables
implementation_tips: Use keyboard navigation (Tab, Arrow keys, Enter) for accessibility and power users.
Close dropdown on click outside or ESC key to prevent trapping users.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure focus management and ARIA roles (menu, menuitem) are implemented so screen readers announce options correctly. Avoid hiding critical actions only behind dropdowns.
components.original_description: A menu in which options are hidden by default but can be shown by interacting with a button; it differs from a select in that it shows actions or navigation options and is not a form input.

components.description: An empty state guides users when no data exists, reducing confusion and prompting action. It’s essential for rapid prototyping because it turns dead ends into opportunities—keeping users engaged instead of frustrated. Great for vibe coding since it adds polish without heavy logic.
use_cases: Search results with no matches
User’s first visit to a dashboard with no saved items
Empty cart or wishlist in e-commerce apps
New project or folder with no files
implementation_tips: Include a clear call-to-action button (e.g., 'Add your first item')
Use illustrations or icons to soften the experience and reinforce context
Avoid generic messages—personalize based on user role or context
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure screen readers announce the empty state message and actionable elements. Use ARIA labels if icons convey meaning without text.
components.original_description: An indication to the user that there is no data to display in the current view; it often includes an alternative action (e.g. try a different search term).

components.description: Groups related form inputs under a shared label, improving form scannability and user focus. Helps developers quickly structure complex forms without custom layout code, reducing cognitive load for users during data entry.
use_cases: User registration forms with personal info sections
Checkout forms separating shipping and billing details
Settings panels grouping related preferences
Survey forms with thematic question blocks
implementation_tips: Always pair with a <legend> for semantic grouping and screen reader context
Use CSS flex/grid to responsively stack fields inside — avoid fixed widths
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure each fieldset has a descriptive <legend> for screen readers; avoid nesting fieldsets unless absolutely necessary to prevent navigation confusion.
components.original_description: A wrapper for related form fields.

components.description: Represents uploaded or downloadable files (PDFs, images, docs) with visual cues and actions. Helps developers quickly add file handling to forms, dashboards, or content hubs without building from scratch — improves user trust through clear affordances and reduces friction in file workflows.
use_cases: User profile attachments (resumes, avatars)
Invoice or report download sections in admin dashboards
File upload previews in form submissions
Document libraries in SaaS apps
implementation_tips: Show file type icons and size to set user expectations
Include a download button or click-to-open behavior with clear feedback
Use progressive enhancement: fallback to native file input if JS fails
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure keyboard focus and screen reader support for file actions; label buttons clearly (e.g., 'Download PDF') and announce file type/size for assistive tech.
components.original_description: A representation of a file such as an uploaded attachment or a downloadable PDF.

components.description: Enables users to select and submit files from their device with minimal friction. Critical for rapid prototyping of forms, dashboards, or content tools — reduces dev time by handling native OS file dialogs and drag-and-drop intuitively.
use_cases: User profile picture uploads
Document submission in admin dashboards
Media uploads for content management systems
Resume or portfolio file submissions
implementation_tips: Use HTML5 <input type='file'> with accept attribute to filter file types (e.g., accept='.jpg,.png')
Add drag-and-drop support with libraries like react-dropzone for richer UX
Show file preview or progress bar for large uploads to reduce user anxiety
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure keyboard navigation works and screen readers announce file types and upload status. Use ARIA labels for custom drop zones.
components.original_description: An input which allows users to upload a file from their device.

components.description: A footer anchors the bottom of pages with essential legal, copyright, or navigation links, reducing user confusion and reinforcing trust. For rapid prototyping, it’s a plug-and-play component that instantly adds polish and compliance without custom design work.
use_cases: Legal compliance pages (Terms, Privacy, GDPR)
Landing page footers with social links and contact info
E-commerce site footers with shipping/return policies
Blog footers with category or archive links
implementation_tips: Use semantic HTML <footer> tag for SEO and screen readers
Keep links minimal and grouped by purpose (e.g., Legal, Support, Social)
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure all links are keyboard-navigable and have descriptive text. Use ARIA labels if icons are used without text.
components.original_description: Commonly appearing at the bottom of a page or section, a footer is used to display copyright and legal information or links to related content.

components.description: Forms collect user input and submit it to a server, enabling core app functions like signups, searches, and settings. They streamline data entry with clear labels, validation, and feedback — critical for reducing user friction during rapid prototyping or vibe coding.
use_cases: User registration and login flows
Search or filter interfaces
Contact or feedback submission
Checkout or payment data entry
Profile or settings updates
implementation_tips: Use native HTML form elements with semantic attributes (e.g., <label for=...>) for built-in accessibility and browser support.
Add real-time validation and clear error messages to prevent submission failures and improve UX.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure all form fields have associated labels, use ARIA roles where needed, and support keyboard navigation and screen reader announcements for errors and success states.
components.original_description: A grouping of input controls that allow a user to submit information to a server.

components.description: The Header anchors every page with consistent branding and navigation, reducing user cognitive load during rapid prototyping. It enables quick access to core features and reinforces app identity, making it essential for vibe coding where visual continuity drives user trust and flow.
use_cases: Main navigation in dashboards
Brand identity placement in landing pages
Quick access to user account or settings in web apps
implementation_tips: Use sticky positioning to keep navigation always accessible on scroll.
Include a mobile hamburger menu toggle for responsive layouts.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure all navigation links are keyboard-focusable and announce their purpose via ARIA labels. Use semantic HTML like <header> and proper heading hierarchy for screen readers.
components.original_description: An element that appears across the top of all pages on a website or application; it usually contains the site name and main navigation.

components.description: Headings structure content hierarchically, helping users scan and understand page layout quickly. For rapid prototyping, they anchor sections visually and semantically, reducing cognitive load and improving navigation flow during vibe coding.
use_cases: Section headers in dashboards
Onboarding step titles
Blog post or article titles
Form section labels
implementation_tips: Use semantic HTML tags (h1–h6) for SEO and screen reader support
Maintain consistent typography scale across headings for visual harmony
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure proper heading hierarchy (h1 → h2 → h3) for screen readers. Avoid skipping levels and always pair with descriptive content.
components.original_description: A title or caption used to introduce a new section.

components.description: A full-width banner that grabs attention immediately, ideal for setting tone and guiding users toward key actions. Helps developers rapidly prototype landing pages or feature highlights with high visual impact and clear CTAs.
use_cases: Landing page headers with primary call-to-action buttons
Feature announcements on product dashboards
Event or promotion banners on e-commerce sites
implementation_tips: Use responsive images with srcset to ensure fast loading on all devices
Overlay text with semi-transparent backgrounds for readability over busy images
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure sufficient color contrast between text and background; provide alt text for images and ARIA labels for interactive elements.
components.original_description: A large banner, usually appearing as one of the first items on a page; it often contains a full-width image.

components.description: Icons visually communicate function or content at a glance, speeding up user comprehension and reducing cognitive load. For rapid prototyping, they let devs quickly convey actions (like save, delete, share) without text, making interfaces feel intuitive and polished even in early builds.
use_cases: Action buttons in toolbars (e.g., edit, delete, share)
Navigation menus (e.g., home, settings, profile)
Status indicators (e.g., success, warning, loading)
Form field helpers (e.g., password visibility toggle, search magnifier)
implementation_tips: Use consistent size and stroke weight across icons for visual harmony.
Prefer SVGs for scalability and performance; avoid raster images.
Bundle icons in a reusable component with props for size, color, and role.
components.accessibility_notes: Always pair icons with text or ARIA labels for screen readers. Avoid using icons alone to convey critical information.
components.original_description: An icon is a graphic symbol designed to visually indicate the purpose of an interface element.

components.description: Embeds visual content to enhance user engagement and convey information quickly. Critical for rapid prototyping to establish visual hierarchy and emotional tone without writing copy. Improves perceived app quality and reduces cognitive load by replacing text with intuitive visuals.
use_cases: Hero sections on landing pages
Product thumbnails in e-commerce grids
User avatars in profile interfaces
Illustrations in onboarding flows
Social media preview cards
implementation_tips: Use responsive srcset and sizes attributes for optimal loading across devices
Always include alt text for SEO and accessibility, even if decorative
Preload critical images above the fold to avoid layout shifts
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure all images have descriptive alt text; use aria-hidden='true' for purely decorative images to avoid screen reader clutter.
components.original_description: An element for embedding images.

components.description: A form label clearly associates text with input fields, improving usability and accessibility. It helps users quickly understand what data to enter, reducing errors and speeding up form completion — critical for rapid prototyping where clarity trumps decoration.
use_cases: Login and signup forms
Checkout pages with address or payment fields
User profile edit screens
Search filters with dropdowns or checkboxes
implementation_tips: Always pair labels with input IDs using 'for' attributes to ensure screen reader compatibility.
Use consistent typography and spacing to maintain visual hierarchy across forms.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure labels are programmatically associated with inputs and provide sufficient contrast. Avoid placeholder text as the only label — it disappears on focus and harms accessibility.
components.original_description: A text label for form inputs.

components.description: Links let users navigate between pages or jump to sections within a page, enabling intuitive information flow. For rapid prototyping, they’re essential for creating clickable wireframes that feel real without backend logic. Properly styled links improve discoverability and reduce user friction.
use_cases: Navigation menus in dashboards
Call-to-action buttons that redirect to external docs or sign-up pages
In-page anchors for long-form content like FAQs or tutorials
Footer links to legal pages or social media
implementation_tips: Use semantic <a> tags with href attributes for SEO and accessibility
Add visual feedback (e.g., underline on hover, color change) to indicate interactivity
Avoid generic text like 'click here' — use descriptive anchor text for clarity
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure links have sufficient color contrast and are keyboard-navigable. Use aria-labels if the link text is ambiguous out of context.
components.original_description: A link is a reference to a resource. This can be external (e.g. a different web page) or internal (e.g. a specific element in the current document).

components.description: Lists organize related items for quick scanning and navigation, making them essential for rapid prototyping of dashboards, settings, or content feeds. They improve UX by reducing cognitive load and enabling predictable interaction patterns, especially in 'vibe coding' where visual clarity matters more than complex logic.
use_cases: User settings menus
Product feature checklists
Navigation menus in mobile apps
Search results or filtered item displays
implementation_tips: Use semantic HTML tags (ul, ol, dl) for better accessibility and SEO.
Add hover/focus states and keyboard navigation for interactive lists.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure lists are programmatically labeled and navigable via keyboard. Use ARIA roles if custom styling breaks native semantics.
components.original_description: Lists are used for grouping a collection of related items. In HTML there are three types:

components.description: Modals temporarily block interaction with the main interface to focus user attention on critical tasks like form submission or confirmation. They reduce cognitive load by isolating actions, making them ideal for rapid prototyping where clarity and flow matter. Great for 'vibe coding' because they instantly create a sense of purpose and direction.
use_cases: Form submissions (e.g. sign-up, checkout)
Confirmation dialogs (e.g. delete item, cancel action)
Onboarding steps or feature highlights
Image or video lightboxes
implementation_tips: Use ESC key and click-outside to close for intuitive dismissal.
Ensure modal content is keyboard-navigable and focus-trapped.
components.accessibility_notes: Always trap focus inside the modal and announce its opening to screen readers. Include a visible close button and ensure ARIA roles (dialog/alertdialog) are properly set.
components.original_description: A modal is an interface element that appears over other content. It requires an interaction from the user before they can return to whatever is underneath.

components.description: A navigation component organizes links to pages or page sections, enabling users to move through content intuitively. It’s essential for rapid prototyping because it establishes information hierarchy early and reduces user friction—critical for keeping users engaged during vibe coding sessions.
use_cases: Main site menus in dashboards or SaaS apps
In-page anchors for long-form content like documentation or blogs
Mobile bottom bars for quick access to core features
Sidebar menus in admin panels or settings interfaces
implementation_tips: Use semantic HTML (nav, ul, li) for SEO and screen reader compatibility
Highlight active links visually to reduce user confusion
Group related items and limit top-level items to 5–7 for cognitive load
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure keyboard navigation works (tab/enter), use ARIA labels for icons, and maintain sufficient color contrast for link states (hover, focus, active).
components.original_description: A container for navigation links; these can be to other pages (e.g. main site navigation) or to elements within the current page (e.g. a table of contents).

components.description: Pagination breaks large datasets into manageable chunks, improving load times and user focus. It’s essential for apps with lists (e.g., search results, product catalogs) where showing everything at once would overwhelm users or slow performance. Great for rapid prototyping when you need to simulate real-world data volume without building full backends.
use_cases: Product listings in e-commerce apps
Search result pages
Blog or news article archives
User dashboard activity logs
Admin panels with large data tables
implementation_tips: Use cursor-based or offset-based pagination depending on data stability and performance needs.
Always include total page count and current page indicator for user orientation.
Debounce or throttle page navigation clicks to prevent accidental double loads.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure pagination controls are keyboard-navigable and screen-reader friendly with ARIA labels. Announce page changes to assistive tech to maintain context.
components.original_description: Pagination is the process of splitting information over multiple pages instead of showing it all on a single page; also the name for the interface component used for navigating between these pages.

components.description: A click-triggered overlay that surfaces contextual content or actions without navigating away, ideal for rapid prototyping of complex interactions. It improves UX by reducing clutter and keeping users focused on their current task while offering deeper options on demand.
use_cases: Context menus for table rows or list items
Inline form editors or quick settings panels
Action sheets with multiple interactive buttons
Rich media previews (e.g., image + metadata)
implementation_tips: Use portal rendering to avoid z-index and overflow issues
Close on click outside or ESC key for intuitive dismissal
Animate entrance/exit for smoother user experience
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure keyboard navigation (Tab/Shift+Tab) works within the popover and provide ARIA roles (e.g., dialog or menu) for screen readers.
components.original_description: An element that pops up from another element over other content; it differs from a tooltip in that it is usually triggered via click instead of hover and can contain interactive elements.

components.description: Visually communicates task completion in real time, reducing user anxiety during long operations like file uploads or data syncs. Helps developers quickly signal system status without cluttering the UI, making apps feel more responsive and trustworthy during async processes.
use_cases: File uploads in cloud storage apps
Data synchronization in offline-first mobile apps
Installation or update progress in desktop software
Form submission with multi-step validation
implementation_tips: Use CSS transitions or animation libraries for smooth visual updates to avoid jarring jumps.
Pair with a percentage label or estimated time remaining for clarity, especially for long tasks.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure the progress value is exposed via ARIA attributes (aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax) so screen readers can announce progress accurately.
components.original_description: A horizontal bar indicating the current completion status of a long-running task, usually updated continuously as the task progresses, instead of in discrete steps.

components.description: Helps users visualize where they are in a multi-step flow, reducing anxiety and abandonment. Essential for onboarding, checkout, or form-heavy experiences — gives users control and context during long processes. Great for vibe coding because it’s visually intuitive and requires minimal setup to feel polished.
use_cases: Checkout flows in e-commerce apps
Onboarding wizards for SaaS products
Multi-step forms (e.g., loan applications, event registrations)
Tutorial sequences in mobile apps
implementation_tips: Use clear, consistent labels for each step and highlight the current step with color or icon
Animate transitions between steps for smoother user experience
Persist progress state across sessions if the flow spans multiple visits
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure keyboard navigation between steps and screen reader support via ARIA labels. Use semantic HTML (like <ol> or <nav>) and indicate current step with aria-current='step'.
components.original_description: A representation of a user’s progress through a series of discrete steps.

components.description: Quotes visually elevate key messages or external citations, improving scannability and emotional impact in content-heavy apps. Ideal for rapid prototyping to add emphasis without redesigning layouts, helping users quickly grasp core ideas or testimonials.
use_cases: Testimonial sections on landing pages
Highlighting key takeaways in blog posts or documentation
Displaying customer feedback in dashboards
Pulling out impactful lines in long-form articles
implementation_tips: Use semantic HTML <blockquote> for SEO and accessibility
Apply subtle visual styling (e.g., left border, italic font) to distinguish from body text without overwhelming
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure quotes are programmatically associated with their source (via <cite> or aria-label) and maintain sufficient contrast for readability.
components.original_description: Quotes are used to display a quotation: either from a person or another outside source or to highlight a passage of the current document (a pull quote).

components.description: Radio buttons let users pick one option from a mutually exclusive set, reducing cognitive load and preventing invalid states. Ideal for forms, settings, and filters where only one choice is allowed — speeds up prototyping by enforcing clear user decisions.
use_cases: User preference settings (e.g., theme: light/dark/system)
Payment method selection (e.g., credit card, PayPal, Apple Pay)
Survey or quiz questions with single-answer choices
Filtering content by category (e.g., ‘All’, ‘Active’, ‘Completed’)
implementation_tips: Group related radio buttons under a single <fieldset> with a <legend> for semantic structure.
Use unique name attributes per group to ensure only one can be selected at a time.
Add visual feedback (e.g., color change or border highlight) on selection for better UX.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure each radio button has a descriptive label linked via ‘for’/‘id’, and use ARIA roles if dynamically generated. Keyboard navigation (Tab + Arrow keys) must work for all options.
components.original_description: Radio buttons allow a user to select a single option from a list of predefined options.

components.description: Allows users to quickly assess or assign value via star ratings, boosting engagement and trust in e-commerce, reviews, or feedback flows. Ideal for rapid prototyping where visual feedback matters — users instantly grasp quality or popularity without reading text.
use_cases: Product detail pages in e-commerce apps
User review sections in service marketplaces
Feedback forms after customer support interactions
App store-style rating prompts post-use
implementation_tips: Use SVG or icon fonts for scalable, crisp stars across devices.
Add hover and click states to indicate interactivity — especially important for touchscreens.
Store and display fractional ratings (e.g., 4.3 stars) for accuracy without cluttering UI.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure keyboard navigation and screen reader support by labeling each star with ARIA roles and values. Announce the current rating when focused or changed.
pairs_well_with: Badge or label showing total ratings
Sort dropdown for filtering by rating
components.original_description: Ratings let users see and/or set a star rating for a product or other item.

components.description: Enables users to format text with bold, lists, links, and more without coding — ideal for content-heavy apps like blogs or CMS dashboards. Speeds up prototyping by letting non-devs edit live content, reducing back-and-forth with designers.
use_cases: Blog post creation in CMS interfaces
User-generated content fields (e.g. forum posts, comments)
Product description editors in e-commerce admin panels
Internal documentation or knowledge base editors
implementation_tips: Use a lightweight library like Tiptap or Quill to avoid bloat.
Sanitize output to prevent XSS attacks when rendering user-submitted HTML.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure keyboard navigation works for toolbar buttons and screen reader compatibility by using ARIA roles. Provide text alternatives for icons and maintain focus order.
components.original_description: An interface for editing “rich text” content (i.e. with formatting), usually through a WYSIWYG interface.

components.description: A search input lets users quickly filter or locate content by typing keywords, reducing friction in content-heavy apps. It’s essential for rapid prototyping because it’s universally understood and instantly improves discoverability without complex navigation.
use_cases: Product catalogs in e-commerce apps
User directories in admin dashboards
Help centers or FAQ sections
File or note search in productivity apps
implementation_tips: Debounce input events to avoid excessive API calls during typing.
Show a clear ‘X’ button to reset the field and improve usability.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure the input has a visible focus state and proper ARIA labels. Screen readers should announce the search function and results dynamically.
components.original_description: Search inputs allow users to find content by entering a search term.

components.description: Segmented controls let users toggle between mutually exclusive views or filters with minimal UI clutter. They’re perfect for rapid prototyping because they’re intuitive, compact, and reduce cognitive load by visually grouping related actions. Great for switching data views, filtering lists, or toggling modes without modal dialogs.
use_cases: Filtering product lists by category (e.g., 'All', 'Electronics', 'Clothing')
Switching between time ranges in dashboards (e.g., 'Today', 'This Week', 'This Month')
Toggling between map and list views in location-based apps
Selecting content types in media apps (e.g., 'Movies', 'TV Shows', 'Podcasts')
implementation_tips: Use CSS transitions or animations to smoothly highlight the active segment for visual feedback.
Ensure the active state is clearly distinguishable via color, border, or shadow — avoid relying solely on text weight.
Bind segment changes to route or state updates for SPA navigation or dynamic content rendering.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure keyboard navigation (Tab + Arrow keys) works and each segment has an ARIA role of 'radio' within a 'radiogroup'. Announce state changes to screen readers using aria-live or aria-selected.
components.original_description: A hybrid somewhere between a button group, radio buttons, and tabs; segmented controls are used to switch between different options or views.

components.description: A compact, intuitive way to let users choose from a predefined list without cluttering the UI. Ideal for rapid prototyping because it’s universally understood and reduces input errors by constraining choices. Enhances UX by minimizing cognitive load and speeding up form completion.
use_cases: Country or state selectors in checkout forms
Filtering data tables by category or status
Setting user preferences like theme or language
Selecting time zones or date ranges
implementation_tips: Pre-select a sensible default to reduce friction for first-time users.
Use semantic HTML <select> with <option> for native accessibility and keyboard support.
Add a searchable variant if the list exceeds 10 items to improve usability.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure keyboard navigation (arrow keys, Enter) works and screen readers announce selected values. Use ARIA attributes if custom-styled to maintain semantics.
components.original_description: A form input used for selecting a value: when collapsed it shows the currently selected option and when expanded, it shows a scrollable list of predefined options for the user to choose from.

components.description: A thin horizontal line that visually groups or divides content, helping users scan layouts faster. Essential for rapid prototyping to create clear visual hierarchy without clutter. Reduces cognitive load by signaling content boundaries in forms, lists, or navigation.
use_cases: Dividing sections in settings or profile pages
Separating items in a list or card grid
Breaking up form fields or multi-step flows
Delimiting header/footer from main content
implementation_tips: Use CSS border or hr tag with consistent height and color for theme alignment
Add padding above/below to avoid visual crowding
Avoid overuse — limit to 1-2 per screen section for clarity
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure sufficient contrast against background; avoid using separators as sole visual cues for grouping — pair with semantic HTML or ARIA labels where needed.
components.original_description: A separator between two elements, usually consisting of a horizontal line.

components.description: Skeleton loaders provide visual feedback during content loading, reducing perceived wait time and improving user retention. They’re ideal for rapid prototyping — developers can mock layouts without real data, maintaining flow while APIs are built. Users feel the app is responsive, even when data isn’t ready.
use_cases: Product listing pages with image + text cards
Dashboard widgets loading analytics data
Profile pages with avatars, stats, and bios
Search results before API returns matches
implementation_tips: Animate skeleton pulses subtly — avoid distracting motion
Match skeleton dimensions to final content to prevent layout shifts
Use CSS-only skeletons for lightweight performance
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure screen readers skip skeleton elements by using aria-hidden='true' — they’re visual placeholders, not interactive content. Don’t rely on them for critical info delivery.
components.original_description: A placeholder layout for content which hasn't yet loaded, usually built up of grey boxes.

components.description: A hidden-but-focusable link that lets keyboard users jump past repetitive navigation to main content, drastically improving accessibility and reducing tabbing fatigue. Essential for rapid prototyping when you need to validate flow without building full navigation logic.
use_cases: Main navigation menus on landing pages
Long forms with multiple sections
Dashboard layouts with persistent sidebars
E-commerce product pages with filters and reviews
implementation_tips: Use CSS to hide the link visually but keep it focusable (e.g., 'position: absolute; left: -9999px; &:focus { left: 16px; }')
Place it as the first focusable element in the DOM for immediate keyboard access
components.accessibility_notes: Must be focusable and visible on focus to meet WCAG. Ensure it targets a meaningful landmark (e.g., main, region, or heading) for screen reader users.
components.original_description: Links within a page for skipping to another section, primarily for users who navigate using a keyboard.

components.description: A slider lets users intuitively select a value within a defined range—perfect for adjusting settings like volume, brightness, or price filters. It reduces cognitive load by replacing manual input with tactile, visual control, speeding up prototyping for interactive dashboards or settings panels.
use_cases: Adjusting media playback volume or brightness
Filtering products by price range in e-commerce
Setting timer durations in productivity apps
Controlling brush size in drawing tools
implementation_tips: Always display the current value visibly next to the slider for clarity.
Use step increments to prevent overly granular or unusable values.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure keyboard navigation (arrow keys) and screen reader support by labeling with ARIA attributes and providing a visible value indicator.
components.original_description: A form control for choosing a value within a preset range of values.

components.description: A spinner provides immediate visual feedback that an action is processing, preventing user frustration during async operations. It’s essential for rapid prototyping to simulate loading states without blocking the UI, helping developers validate flow before backend integration.
use_cases: Form submissions with API calls
Data fetching in dashboards or lists
Image or video uploads
Page transitions with dynamic content
implementation_tips: Always pair with a timeout or error state to avoid infinite spinners.
Use CSS animations or SVG for lightweight, smooth performance.
components.accessibility_notes: Announce loading states via ARIA live regions so screen readers inform users. Avoid relying solely on visual cues.
components.original_description: A visual indicator that a process is happening in the background but the interface is not yet ready for interaction.

components.description: Stack simplifies vertical or horizontal spacing between UI elements by applying consistent margins, reducing manual CSS tuning. It accelerates prototyping by enforcing visual rhythm and improving layout consistency across screens, especially during 'vibe coding' where rapid iteration matters.
use_cases: Form fields with consistent vertical spacing
Card lists in dashboards or feeds
Navigation menus with evenly spaced items
Onboarding steps with visual separation
implementation_tips: Set default spacing via theme tokens for design system consistency
Use responsive spacing props to adapt to mobile breakpoints
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure focus order remains logical when stacking interactive elements; avoid using Stack to group semantically related controls that should be in a native list or group for screen readers.
components.original_description: A wrapper component for adding a consistent margin between components.

components.description: A compact, intuitive control for adjusting numeric values via increment/decrement buttons — perfect for rapid prototyping of forms, carts, or settings. Reduces input errors by constraining values and offering tactile feedback, improving UX in quantity selectors or numeric settings.
use_cases: Shopping cart quantity selectors
Age or guest count inputs in booking flows
Adjusting font size or volume in settings panels
Configuring timer durations in productivity apps
implementation_tips: Set min/max bounds to prevent invalid states and reduce validation logic.
Add keyboard arrow key support for power users and accessibility.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure screen readers announce value changes and label buttons clearly (e.g., 'Increase quantity'). Use ARIA attributes to reflect current value and step size.
components.original_description: A control for editing a numeric value with buttons for decrementing / incrementing.

components.description: A data table lets developers quickly display structured datasets with built-in sorting and filtering, reducing dev time for admin panels or analytics dashboards. It improves user efficiency by letting users scan, compare, and manipulate data without custom logic.
use_cases: Admin dashboards showing user or order lists
Analytics reports with sortable metrics
Inventory or CRM systems with bulk actions
Comparison tables for pricing or feature matrices
implementation_tips: Use virtual scrolling for large datasets to maintain performance
Expose column visibility toggles and persistent sorting state via URL or localStorage
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure keyboard navigation (tab, arrow keys) works across rows and columns, and use ARIA labels for sortable headers and screen reader announcements.
components.original_description: A component for displaying large amounts of data in rows and columns; commonly referred to as a 'Data Table' when it includes sorting and/ or filtering functionality.

components.description: Tabs let users switch between distinct content panels without leaving the page, ideal for organizing dense information in dashboards or settings. Multi-step forms broken into logical sections

Lazy-load tab content to improve initial load performance.
Highlight active tab with clear visual feedback (e.g., underline, color change).
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure keyboard navigation (Tab, Arrow keys) works between tabs and that screen readers announce tab state. Use ARIA attributes to link tabs to their panels.
components.original_description: Tabbed interfaces are a way of navigating between multiple panels, reducing clutter and fitting more into a smaller space.

components.description: A single-line text field that lets users enter short strings like names, emails, or search terms. Search bars in dashboards
Filter inputs in data tables
Quick note or tag entry in task apps
implementation_tips: Add placeholder text to guide users without cluttering the UI.
Use native HTML input types (email, tel, etc.) for better mobile keyboard behavior.
Validate input on blur or submit to avoid interrupting user flow.
components.accessibility_notes: Always pair with a visible label using 'for' and 'id' attributes. Ensure focus states are visually clear and support keyboard navigation.
components.original_description: A form control that accepts a single line of text.

components.description: A multi-line text input that lets users write or edit longer content like feedback, descriptions, or code. Essential for rapid prototyping because it’s universally supported, requires no complex setup, and instantly improves UX by allowing natural, unconstrained input.

Product or blog post descriptions
Code or configuration input fields
Support ticket details
implementation_tips: Set a reasonable rows attribute (e.g., 4–6) to avoid overwhelming users or wasting space.
Add placeholder text to guide input format or expectations.
components.accessibility_notes: Always pair with a visible label using 'for' and 'id', and ensure it’s keyboard-navigable. Use aria-describedby for helper text if needed.
components.original_description: A form control for editing multi-line text.

components.description: A transient, non-blocking notification that appears briefly above content to confirm actions or deliver status updates without interrupting user flow. Ideal for rapid prototyping because it’s lightweight, requires no user dismissal, and enhances perceived responsiveness in apps.

Notifying users of network errors or offline states
Showing success/failure of async operations (e.g., 'Image uploaded')
Displaying undo options after deletions
implementation_tips: Auto-dismiss after 3–5 seconds to avoid clutter
Use consistent positioning (bottom-center on mobile, top-right on desktop)
Support keyboard dismissal (Escape key) for accessibility
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure toast messages are announced by screen readers via ARIA live regions, and avoid using color alone to convey status (e.g., pair icons with text).
components.original_description: A type of alert which appears in a layer above other content, visually similar to a mobile or desktop push notification.

components.description: A toggle lets users instantly switch between two states (like on/off or enabled/disabled) with a single tap or click. Feature flags in admin dashboards
Filter toggles in data tables or search interfaces
Enabling/disabling integrations or sync options
implementation_tips: Use clear visual feedback (color, animation, or label change) to confirm state change.
Ensure the toggle’s label is always visible and describes the action (e.g., 'Enable Auto-Save').
components.accessibility_notes: Always pair toggles with ARIA attributes (role='switch', aria-checked) and ensure keyboard navigation (Tab + Space/Enter) works. Screen readers should announce the current state clearly.
components.original_description: A control used to switch between two states: often on or off.

components.description: Tooltips provide contextual help or microcopy without cluttering the UI, making them ideal for rapid prototyping where space is tight. They improve user understanding of icons, buttons, or complex fields without requiring extra screen real estate or modal dialogs.

Form field hints for validation or formatting
Data visualization labels on hover
Accessibility labels for non-text elements
implementation_tips: Use CSS transitions for smooth fade-in/out to avoid jarring UX
Debounce hover events to prevent flickering on fast mouse movements
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure tooltips are keyboard-navigable and announced by screen readers; avoid using them for critical info that must always be visible.
components.original_description: A means of displaying a description or extra information about an element, usually on hover, but can also be on click or tap.

components.description: Tree views let users navigate nested data like folders, categories, or settings with expand/collapse controls. They reduce cognitive load by hiding depth until needed, making complex hierarchies feel manageable during rapid prototyping or vibe coding.

Settings menus with subcategories
Product category navigation in e-commerce
Org charts or team structures
Documentation or API reference TOCs
implementation_tips: Use keyboard navigation (arrow keys, Enter) for accessibility and power-user efficiency.
Persist expanded/collapsed state per user session to avoid re-navigation fatigue.
components.accessibility_notes: Ensure all nodes are focusable and announce expanded/collapsed state via ARIA. Support screen reader navigation through hierarchical levels.
components.original_description: A component for displaying nested hierarchical information, such as a table of contents or directory structure.

components.description: Video players let users watch and control media playback directly in-app, enhancing engagement without leaving the interface. Ideal for rapid prototyping of tutorials, demos, or marketing content where motion conveys value faster than static text or images.

User-generated content feeds (e.g., social or review apps)

components.accessibility_notes: Always include captions and ensure keyboard navigation (play/pause, volume, seek) works. Provide transcript links for screen reader users.

components.description: This component hides text visually but keeps it accessible to screen readers, helping developers quickly add context without cluttering the UI. Ideal for vibe coding where you want to maintain accessibility while iterating fast on visual layouts.

components.accessibility_notes: Ensure visually hidden text is meaningful and not redundant. Test with screen readers to confirm it’s announced correctly and doesn’t disrupt the user flow.
